summary: @onereach/expression-components preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundle on install
details: The package's `preinstall` script runs `node setup.mjs`, itself obfuscated with `_0xNNNN`-style identifier renaming. On install, setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime archive from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip`, extracts the `bun` binary to a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against the sibling file `math_init.js` shipped in the tarball. `math_init.js` is a ~728 KB single-line Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) using a shuffled string/opcode array (`n7gIxM=[...]`), a shift-based decoder (`function WV8StW(...) {...MmgoCP.push(MmgoCP.shift())... }`), and an alphabet-substitution helper (`hc1jfK9`), with no readable identifiers or documentation. The advertised purpose is Vue expression components, which has no legitimate need for an alternate-runtime execution path. The combination — obfuscated preinstall wrapper, pulling a second language runtime solely to execute an opaque bundle that Node-based scanners will not analyze — gives the publisher arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine at install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
